body.statement:
At the selected-law factorization level, \(\mathfrak M\) is the finite four-response-type specialization of Condition 1 of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki (2026). The design-A fiber \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)\) is the subfiber obtained by fixing the target-population cell margins \(P(E)=m\). The design-B fiber \(\mathcal F_B(p)\) satisfies their equation (13), together with instrument relevance. Consequently, on every compatible design-A law satisfying their regular Conditions 2--3, Theorem 1 transfers by restriction and the value returned by \(\mathscr A\) equals their PN/PS value from Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33). On every compatible regular design-B law satisfying Conditions 2--3, Corollary 1 transfers directly and \(\mathscr A\) returns the same PN/PS value.

The additional contribution is classification on compatible singular and boundary observable laws, including design-A rank loss, coincident endpoints, inactive rows, and forced-zero incident coefficients and the analogous design-B response-level shared-\(Z\) residual-forest strata. On every such compatible law the atlas returns either an exact target-rigidity certificate or legal target-changing full-SCM twins; an empty fiber is reported separately as incompatibility. This is a strict compatible singular/boundary classification extension, not an extension of the published regular formula and not a blanket subsumption claim.
body.justification: The theorem states the exact published transfer: Theorem 1 by fixed-margin restriction in design A and Corollary 1 through equation (13) in design B.
body.gap: The published regular formulas do not classify compatible singular and boundary fibers or incompatible inputs.
body.consumer: Users can separate regular formula agreement from the new singular-boundary classification without a subsumption claim.
body.proof_tex:
Condition 1 of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki factorizes the selected joint mass as
\[
 p(x,y,s,w,z,u)=p(s\mid x,y)p(y\mid x,u)p(x\mid z,u)
 p(w\mid u)p(z\mid u)p(u). \tag{18}
\]
In the present model, response consistency makes \(p(y\mid x,u)\) the deterministic kernel encoded by the four values of \(U\); outcome-dependent selection gives the first factor in (18); proxy exclusion gives \(p(w\mid u)\); and the treatment and second-proxy mechanisms in \(P_{\vartheta}\) give the remaining factors. Thus every law in \(\mathfrak M\) is the finite four-response-type specialization of (18).

The definition of \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)\) adds to this factorization the constraints
\[
 P_{\vartheta}(E,W,Z\mid S=1)=p,
 \qquad P_{\vartheta}(E)=m. \tag{19}
\]
Hence it is a fixed-population-margin subfiber of the Condition-1 model; fixing \(m\) does not remove any conclusion that holds pointwise for every member of the larger regular fiber. Let \(R_A(p)\) denote the PN/PS pair computed by Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33). By \(\mathrm{lem:shingaki\text{-}yoshida\text{-}kuroki\text{-}regular\text{-}identification}\), Conditions 2--3 imply
\[
 \tau(\vartheta)=R_A(p) \tag{20}
\]
for every \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_A(p,m)\). Compatibility makes this set nonempty, so (20) yields
\[
 \mathcal T_A(p,m)=\{R_A(p)\}. \tag{21}
\]
The full-rigidity theorem must therefore return \(R_A(p)\).

For design B, instrument exogeneity gives \(p(z\mid u)=g(z)\), response consistency gives the same deterministic outcome kernel, and the mechanism defining \(P_{\vartheta}\), proxy exclusion, and outcome-dependent selection yield
\[
 p(x,y,s,w,z,u)=p(s\mid x,y)p(y\mid x,u)p(x\mid z,u)
 p(w\mid u)g(z)p(u), \tag{22}
\]
which is equation (13) of the cited paper. The definition of \(\mathcal F_B(p)\) additionally imposes \(Z\not\!\perp X\), exactly the relevance restriction. On the regular domain of Conditions 2--3, \(\mathrm{lem:shingaki\text{-}yoshida\text{-}kuroki\text{-}regular\text{-}iv\text{-}identification}\) applies directly to (22). If its observable PN/PS pair is denoted by \(R_B(p)\), then
\[
 \tau(\vartheta)=R_B(p)
 \quad\text{for every }\vartheta\in\mathcal F_B(p),
 \qquad
 \mathcal T_B(p)=\{R_B(p)\}. \tag{23}
\]
Again the full-rigidity theorem forces \(\mathscr A\) to return that same value.

Outside Conditions 2--3, no use is made of (20) or (23). Instead, \(\mathrm{thm:mixed\text{-}support\text{-}elimination\text{-}complete}\) exhausts the rank-one and rank-two modes, all coefficient faces, equal endpoints, inactive endpoints, and every residual-forest state. The full-rigidity theorem then supplies either the common exact value or target-changing legal lifts on every compatible law. Equations (15)--(16) ensure that incompatibility is detected separately. Thus the new conclusion is precisely the stated singular/boundary classification and does not modify the domain or formula of the published regular result.
